excerpt: At Time 2, planned contrasts for alerting found no significant MBSR-control difference, but the collapsed control and MBSR groups differed from the retreat group in RT scores [t(1,49) = 3.55, p < .001]. No-cue RTs were significantly shorter in the younger retreat group than in the control plus MBSR group [t(1,40) = 2.17, p = .03], whereas double-cue RTs were not significantly different.
overview: This result supports the interpretation that retreat participation altered alerting-related performance by improving target detection when no temporal or spatial cue was available. The double-cue non-difference narrows the effect to no-cue readiness rather than a general speed advantage across alerting conditions. The evidence is strongest for the younger retreat subgroup when explicit RT comparisons are made because the full retreat group had broader age variation.
title: Retreat Alerting Contrast
